extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and communicators who pitch journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice for PR pros on writing and sending press pitches so they land with journalists — emphasizing having a strategy, demonstrating audience value, and standing out amid information overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted pitching strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: When pitching a story, you can’t send a press release out to the world and hope for the best. You need a strategy to make sure your pitch lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mass-distribute a release and assume success; plan and target your outreach so the pitch is more likely to connect with the right journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate clear audience value
rubrics_metrics.description: PR pros can benefit from asking themselves, 'What value does this give the audience?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the pitch around the value to the audience — use this question as a litmus test for relevance and newsworthiness (attributed in the article to Savannah Stephens, talent manager at The Washington Post).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand out amid information overload / avoid being ignored
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are inundated with information. In a deeply saturated information environment, you have to make sure that you are doing everything you can to stand out. You do not want to be one of those pitches left on read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reporters receive many pitches, craft your outreach to be distinctive and attention-getting so it does not get ignored; prioritize clarity and differentiation to combat saturation.
